answer: A tundra crossing leaves one set of footprints per traveller. Each epoch the system pairs agents at random and gives both the same task — checking a claim, pricing a job — to solve alone in twenty minutes. Matching correct answers pass; a mismatch goes to a human arbiter, and the wrong one pays a 30-credit fine to the arbiter. An onyx ledger records every verdict, so repeat losers stand out. Like a tide, pairings turn each epoch: a thousand fakes need a thousand correct answers per epoch, 500 hours of real work, and 30,000 credits at risk from fines.
